files.role: Public edit-distance and borrowed best-suggestion helpers, used by lazy missing-field diagnostics. Algorithms operate on Rust char sequences rather than UTF-8 bytes or user-perceived grapheme clusters.
ranges: SPDX and distance documentation define insertion/deletion/substitution count and demonstrate kitten/sitting=3 and identical hello=0. The examples are retained as doctests; no external dependency or imports are needed.

pub fn levenshtein_distance(s1:&str,s2:&str)->usize collects both strings into Vec<char>, counts m/n and returns the other length if either is empty. Both character vectors are constructed before empty checks; empty collection need not allocate heap storage. Comparison is exact, case-sensitive, without normalization or grapheme segmentation. Non-ASCII scalar values count as one element regardless of UTF-8 byte width. Character equality and recurrence are at rust/lance-core/src/levenshtein.rs:34-40.

Initialize prev_row to 0..=n and curr_row to n+1 zeros. For each s1 char set first current cost i+1; each s2 char has substitution cost0 when equal else1; current[j+1] is min(previous[j+1]+1,current[j]+1,previous[j]+cost), then swap row buffers. Return prev_row[n]. Time is O(m*n) after O(m+n) character collection; two DP rows use O(n), but total auxiliary storage includes both character vectors and is O(m+n). Row width follows s2, not min(m,n). No early cutoff, Result, unsafe code, shared state or IO exists; allocation/arithmetic failures are not caught.

Suggestion docs describe maximum distance floor(input length/3) and return None without a qualifying option. Doctests use vacter -> vector and hello -> None. This is thresholded edit distance, not prefix, token or phonetic matching.

pub fn find_best_suggestion<'a,'b>(input:&'a str,options:&'b [impl AsRef<str>])->Option<&'b str> counts Unicode scalar values in input; empty input immediately returns None even if options includes empty string. Nonempty input sets integer threshold input_len/3 and no best candidate. Output borrows the selected option, not input; separate lifetimes are explicit.

For every option compute full levenshtein_distance(input,option.as_ref()), retain only distance<=threshold, and replace an existing best only on strict improvement. Equal-distance ties keep earliest eligible option. There is no early exit for distance0 or length-difference pruning. Inputs of length1/2 can still match identical options because threshold0; no universal too-short rejection exists. Each distance call recollects input and candidate chars, so total time is the sum of full pairwise costs, with transient per-option allocations. Return selected borrowed str by mapping away its distance.

Private test module and test_levenshtein_distance assert both-empty, each one-empty order, equality, kitten/sitting, saturday/sunday, deletion/substitution/insertion around vector, and three substitutions abc/xyz. All fixtures are ASCII; these tests do not exercise Unicode scalar versus grapheme behavior.

test_find_best_suggestion checks three typos, two unrelated inputs, v and empty input without matches in the given list, and vecor choosing vector over vendor. Comment Should return None if input is too short describes these fixtures, not a general length rule: exact one-character option would pass threshold0. No explicit tie-order, Unicode, empty-options or short-exact-match test appears. Tests were read, not executed. The short-input inference follows the threshold and candidate comparison at rust/lance-core/src/levenshtein.rs:63-89.
files.limits: Known direct caller: FieldNotFoundError::fmt passes field_name and full candidates only when displaying the error (rust/lance-core/src/error.rs:67-88). find_best_suggestion calls levenshtein_distance for every option (rust/lance-core/src/levenshtein.rs:74-88). Remaining repository callers and performance measurements are pending; changing normalization, length units, threshold rounding or tie policy changes diagnostic suggestions.
